proof.text: Put $\mathcal M_S=\operatorname{Mod}(A_S)$ and write $r_N:N\to j_*j^*N$ and $k_N:F(N)\to N$. Kernels in these categories are sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. If $V\to U$ is a pro-etale object, then $V\times_T U=V$ canonically, and the direct-image formula of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] identifies $r_N(V)$ with the identity of $N(V)$. Since $j^*$ is restriction by hypothesis, $j^*F(N)=0$. For $a:N\to N'$, naturality of $r$ gives a unique map $F(a)$ with $k_{N'}F(a)=ak_N$; uniqueness proves the functor identities and $F(a+b)=F(a)+F(b)$. The exact transported inverse image $i^*$ of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] is additive, hence so is $H=i^*F$. Denote by $\theta_N:F(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*H(N)$ the closed unit, an isomorphism by the supported-unit hypothesis. Naturality of that unit makes $\theta$ natural. Thus $e_N=k_N\theta_N^{-1}:i_*H(N)\to N$ is natural.

source.place: First sentence: the sheaf-level supported functor; explicit sectionwise kernel calculation

proof.text: For $h:i_*M\to N$, naturality of $r$ gives $r_Nh=j_*j^*(h)r_{i_*M}=0$, because $j^*i_*M=0$ by hypothesis. The kernel property gives a unique $\bar h:i_*M\to F(N)$ with $k_N\bar h=h$. Full faithfulness of $i_*$ gives a unique $g:M\to H(N)$ with $i_*g=\theta_N\bar h$. Conversely send $g$ to $e_N i_*g$. Starting from $h$, this returns $k_N\bar h=h$. Starting from $g$, the kernel factor of $e_N i_*g$ is $\theta_N^{-1}i_*g$, so full faithfulness returns $g$. These inverse bijections are natural: precomposition is respected by the unique kernel factor and the unique fully faithful lift, and postcomposition is respected by naturality of $k$ and $\theta$. This constructs $i_*\dashv H$. The inverse bijection sends $1_{H(N)}$ to $e_N$, so its counit is precisely the claimed supported-unit inverse followed by the kernel inclusion. Every map is a morphism of left module sheaves; no multiplication of coefficients is interchanged.

source.place: First sentence, identification of the sheaf right adjoint: kernel factorization and the explicit counit

proof.text: Both adjoints are additive: $H$ was checked above and $i_*$ is additive by its sectionwise direct-image formula. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] to $v=i_*$ and $u=H$. It gives an adjunction on homotopy categories whose counit at a complex $I$ is the class of the chain map $e_I=(e_{I^q})_q$. In particular this is a chain map, not merely a list of sheaf morphisms. Since the left adjoint $i_*$ is exact by hypothesis, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] applies to this same sheaf adjunction and shows that $H(I)$ is K-injective whenever $I$ is K-injective. Its exact-left-adjoint hypothesis is satisfied on the whole abelian category, with no boundedness restriction.

proof.text: For each $S=T,Z$, the site and ring sheaf in the statement are small relative to the chosen module universe. The arbitrary-ring theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] therefore makes $\mathcal M_S$ Grothendieck abelian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-functorial-existence] to obtain a quasi-isomorphism from every complex of $\mathcal M_S$ to a K-injective complex. This applies to the left $A_S$-module categories even when $A$ is noncommutative: the first cited statement expressly has no commutativity assumption, and the second is a theorem for any Grothendieck abelian category. Consequently every object of either ordinary unbounded derived category can be represented by a K-injective complex.

Let $H_h:K(\mathcal M_T)\to K(\mathcal M_Z)$ denote the termwise functor from step 3. To check the exactness hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], use the cone and shift formulas of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Additivity identifies $H(\operatorname{Cone}(f))^q$ with $H(L^q)\oplus H(K^{q+1})$ and its differential with $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}H(d_L)&H(f)\\0&-H(d_K)\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, the differential of $\operatorname{Cone}(H(f))$. It preserves the inclusion and minus-projection of the cone triangle, and $H(-d)=-H(d)$ identifies shifts. Thus $H_h$ carries cone triangles to cone triangles. By [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated], these generate the distinguished triangles and $Q_Z$ is exact. Hence $Q_ZH_h$ is an exact functor of triangulated categories in the sense of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Step 4 supplies enough K-injectives, so [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] gives $RH$ and its natural comparison $\beta_C:Q_ZH(C)\to RH(Q_TC)$, with $\beta_I$ invertible for every K-injective $I$. This is the asserted computation $RH(Q_TI)=Q_ZH(I)$ under that comparison.

By exactness of $i_*$ and [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], termwise pushforward descends to $i_*^D$, with the canonical comparison $a_M:i_*^D(Q_ZM)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_T(i_*M)$. For an arbitrary complex $M$ on $Z$ and a K-injective $I$ on $T$, the K-injectivity of $I$ and $H(I)$ from step 3 permits two applications of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Together with [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] they give bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T)}(i_*^D Q_ZM,Q_TI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(T)}(i_*M,I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(Z)}(M,H(I))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Z)}(Q_ZM,Q_ZH(I)).$$
Here the first bijection uses $a_M$; the middle one is exactly the sheaf adjunction lifted in step 3. Postcomposing the last Hom set by $\beta_I$ gives the desired Hom set with target $RH(Q_TI)$. Explicitly, a homotopy class $[h]:i_*M\to I$ is sent to $\beta_I\,Q_Z(\operatorname{adj}(h))$.

The preceding bijections are natural on complexes by the termwise adjunction. For a chain map $f:I\to I'$ between K-injectives, naturality of the derived comparison says $RH(Q_Tf)\beta_I=\beta_{I'}Q_ZH(f)$, so they are also natural in the resolved target. Every derived morphism between such targets comes from a unique homotopy class by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], hence this checks all target morphisms. In the source variable the same naturality equation holds for every chain map. Both sides send a quasi-isomorphism in that variable to a bijection: $Q_Z$ inverts it and the functor $i_*^D$ preserves isomorphisms. Naturality therefore holds for inverses of these maps as well, and hence for all morphisms of the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Finally, step 4 gives a K-injective representative for every target object. Transport along such representatives is independent of the representative, since the induced isomorphism between any two representatives is already among the target morphisms just checked. We have a bifunctorial Hom bijection on the two full derived categories, which is the adjunction $i_*^D\dashv RH$.

proof.text:
Set $M=H(I)$ in step 6. The termwise counit class $[e_I]:i_*H(I)\to I$ is sent by the homotopy adjunction to $[1_{H(I)}]$. Therefore $Q_T(e_I)\,a_{H(I)}$ is sent by our derived Hom bijection to $\beta_I$. By naturality in its first argument, the morphism
$$Q_T(e_I)\,a_{H(I)}\,i_*^D(\beta_I^{-1}):i_*^D RH(Q_TI)\longrightarrow Q_TI$$
is sent to the identity of $RH(Q_TI)$, so it is the derived counit. Under $a$ and $\beta$ this is exactly $Q_T(e_I)$, as claimed. Step 2 identified every component of $e_I$ as $k_{I^q}\theta_{I^q}^{-1}$, so the map is the specified kernel inclusion after the supported-unit isomorphism. Moreover $i_*^D(\beta_I)\,a_{H(I)}^{-1}$ is the asserted canonical identification $Q_Ti_*H(I)\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*^D RH(Q_TI)$. Thus both the object and the arrow agree with the derived-functor comparisons, not just with an unspecified right adjoint.

title: Closed support adjunction and its derived counit
statement:
Let $T$ be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]), let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with quasi-compact complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $A$ be a finite ring, not necessarily commutative. Work in the left module sheaf categories on the small pro-etale sites of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Use their ordinary unbounded derived categories and localization functors $Q_S$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define $F(N)=\ker(N\to j_*j^*N)$ and $H(N)=i^*F(N)$ with the coefficient actions and units of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact].

Assume $i_*$ is exact and fully faithful. Assume also that $j^*$ is restriction, that $j^*i_*M=0$ for every left $A_Z$-module sheaf $M$, and that the closed unit $N\to i_*i^*N$ is an isomorphism for every left $A_T$-module sheaf $N$ with $j^*N=0$.

Then $i_*$ is left adjoint to $H$. Its sheaf counit $i_*H(N)\to N$ is the inverse of the supported unit $F(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*i^*F(N)$ followed by the kernel inclusion. Let $RH$ be the total right derived functor of $H$ [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. For every K-injective complex $I$ (every map from an acyclic complex to $I$ is homotopic to zero [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]), the complex $H(I)$ is K-injective and $RH(Q_TI)=Q_ZH(I)$. Termwise $i_*$ induces a functor $i_*^D$ on the unbounded derived categories; one has $i_*^D\dashv RH$, and its counit at $Q_TI$ is $Q_T(i_*H(I)\to I)$ with the just specified termwise kernel inclusion. In particular $Q_Ti_*H(I)=i_*^D RH(Q_TI)$ under the canonical derived-functor comparisons.
